CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Region of East Halmahera Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of East Halmahera Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of East Halmahera.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Apparatus is a Regional Apparatus whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the affairs of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.

11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

12. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and reasonably both in the family and in society.

17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.

18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to the area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2PTP2A, is the Regional Technical Implementation Unit (UPTDD) of the Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children integrated into the technical Regional Apparatus of East Halmahera Regency.

Article 51

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and child victims of violence is carried out at the end of each Budget year or if necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and child victims of violence are used as input for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and child victims of violence for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 16

1. The implementation of Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of health as referred to in Article 13 letter b, the Regional Government is obliged to provide facilities and organize comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb which is carried out in stages adjusted to the regional financial capacity and supported by community participation.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burdens for malnourished children, children undergoing dialysis due to kidney failure, children with thalassemia major, children with disabilities, children with special needs, street children, children infected with HIV/ AIDS, child workers, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who are victims of violence, such as neglect, economically exploited, sexually exploited and victims of human trafficking.
3. Children as referred to in paragraph (2) are children from poor families except as otherwise regulated in accordance with the health financing program established by the government.

Other violence as referred to in Article 27 letter f is caused by:

a. threat of violence includes: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and

b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF EAST HALMAHERA REGENCY

NUMBER 7 YEAR 2022

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in East Halmahera so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations. So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection measures in the Region so that institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation. Regional Regulations regulate protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in East Halmahera.

CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 50

1. To ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities, protection of Women and children, the Government conducts monitoring.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by technical Regional Apparatus and P2TP2A.
3. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children.
4. Monitoring is carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus implementing policies, activities for the protection of Women and child victims of violence.

(,5i) Monitoring is carried out from planning through to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children every year.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Region of East Halmahera Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of East Halmahera Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of East Halmahera.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Apparatus is a Regional Apparatus whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the affairs of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.

11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

12. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and reasonably both in the family and in society.

17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.

18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to the area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in East Halmahera so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations. So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection measures in the Region so that institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation. Regional Regulations regulate protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in East Halmahera.

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. 2. Women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is directed to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in economic, socio-cultural, political, and legal activities.

CHAPTER X

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 54

1. In the implementation of Protection of Women and children, the community may:
a. form family partners at the Village/Sub-district level by the community;
b. conduct independent socialization of women's and children's rights;
c. provide first aid to victims; and
d. report to the competent authority if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by individuals, community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, private sector and/or mass media.

Article 55

b. Suspension of permit;

3. Suspension of Permit as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is imposed if a written warning has been given as referred to in paragraph (2).
4. Suspension of Permit as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b may be withdrawn if the person or business entity committing the violation pays an administrative fine of Rp. 30,000,000,- (thirty million rupiah).
5. If within the period specified in the permit suspension, the administrative fine is not paid, then the permit will be revoked.

CHAPTER VIII

FINANCING

Article 52

Funding for the implementation of Protection of Women and children, is sourced from:

a. Regional revenue and expenditure budget; and/or
b. Other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 16

1. The implementation of Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of health as referred to in Article 13 letter b, the Regional Government is obliged to provide facilities and organize comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb which is carried out in stages adjusted to the regional financial capacity and supported by community participation.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burdens for malnourished children, children undergoing dialysis due to kidney failure, children with thalassemia major, children with disabilities, children with special needs, street children, children infected with HIV/ AIDS, child workers, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who are victims of violence, such as neglect, economically exploited, sexually exploited and victims of human trafficking.
3. Children as referred to in paragraph (2) are children from poor families except as otherwise regulated in accordance with the health financing program established by the government.

Article 51

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and child victims of violence is carried out at the end of each Budget year or if necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and child victims of violence are used as input for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and child victims of violence for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 50

1. To ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities, protection of Women and children, the Government conducts monitoring.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by technical Regional Apparatus and P2TP2A.
3. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children.
4. Monitoring is carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus implementing policies, activities for the protection of Women and child victims of violence.

(,5i) Monitoring is carried out from planning through to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children every year.

Article 43

1. Social reintegration services as referred to in Article 37 letter f aim to return victims to their families and social environment.
2. Social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:
a. relevant agencies and institutions both government and non-government; and
b. village community institutions and/or local community leaders.

Article 12

1. To carry out women's empowerment as referred to in Article 6, the Regional Government may involve community participation.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, Social Community Institutions, religious institutions and/ or other legitimate institutions.

Article 18

(1) The implementation of Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of education as referred to in Article 13 letter c, the Regional Government guarantees the implementation of a 12 (twelve) year compulsory education program for all children.
